origins: If we see few examples of people from our background in leadership, college, or business, we may conclude that success is for others. Counselors, teachers, or relatives may have lowered expectations, and the statistics we hear can feel like a sentence.
teaches: Scripture is full of unlikely people chosen by God: Joseph the slave, Ruth the foreigner, Esther the orphan, David the youngest son. Paul writes, “God chose the foolish things of the world to shame the wise; God chose the weak things of the world to shame the strong.” He also says, “I can do all things through Christ who gives me strength.” Group statistics describe averages, not individuals. Your future is not determined by where people like you have been.
self_statements: Nobody from my background makes it.
I do not look like the people who succeed.
They will not give me a chance.
errors: Treating group averages as personal destiny.
Noticing the failures and missing the successes.
questions: Who from my background has succeeded, in any field?
Who told me people like me do not succeed?
What strengths and experiences do I bring that others lack?
What barriers are real, and what can I do about them?
What does God say about the people He chooses?
What is one concrete next step?
truth: Group statistics do not decide my future. God often chooses the unlikely, and He gives strength for the road. Real barriers exist, and I can face them with preparation, allies, and perseverance.
hw_truths: I can do all things through Christ.
I am fearfully and wonderfully made.
Barriers are real and can be faced.
My future is not decided by averages.
log: Each week, add one example of someone like you who succeeded.
actions: Find three people from your background who succeeded.
Ask someone further down the road to talk.
Write one specific goal and the next step.
List what stands in the way and who can help.
prayer: Lord, You choose the unlikely. Lift my eyes beyond what I have been told. Give me strength, doors, and allies, and use my story for Your glory. Amen.
hw_questions: Who from my background has succeeded?
name_example: Sarah can write: “God chooses the unlikely, and I can do all things through Christ.”
